A) Reusing the same static password across every device so that Git operations remain simple and consistent to configure
B) A personal access token (or other supported credential) that can be scoped and revoked independently of the account password
C) Disabling authentication entirely for private repositories so that trusted collaborators never need to sign in at all
Back:
B) A personal access token (or other supported credential) that can be scoped and revoked independently of the account password

GitHub requires token-based authentication (PATs, SSH keys, or GitHub App tokens) instead of passwords for Git over HTTPS.

Reference: Managing your personal access tokens - GitHub Docs
Extra: Fine-grained PATs let you scope access to specific repos and permissions and set expirations. SSH keys are another supported option for Git operations.

Front:
What does GitHub Sponsors enable?

A) Automatically distributing a project's advertising revenue equally among every contributor who has ever merged a pull request
B) Providing financial support to open-source developers and organizations directly through their GitHub profiles
C) Selling proprietary closed-source licenses on a developer's behalf and handling all customer billing and support inquiries
Back:
B) Providing financial support to open-source developers and organizations directly through their GitHub profiles

GitHub Sponsors lets the community fund maintainers and projects with recurring or one-time payments.

Reference: About GitHub Sponsors - GitHub Docs
Extra: Sponsorship helps sustain open source financially. It is voluntary funding, not ad revenue sharing or license reselling.

Front:
An enterprise wants to share code internally across all teams to encourage reuse and collaboration, following an InnerSource model. Which approach supports this?

A) Marking every internal project as a public repository so that external contributors can also participate and reuse the code
B) Restricting each project to a single private repository that only its immediate team members are permitted to view
C) Using internal repositories so all enterprise members can view and contribute, applying open-source practices inside the company
Back:
C) Using internal repositories so all enterprise members can view and contribute, applying open-source practices inside the company

Internal repositories enable InnerSource: open-source-style collaboration visible to the whole enterprise but not the public.

Reference: GitHub Docs
Extra: InnerSource brings open-source transparency and reuse inside an organization. Public exposes code externally; strictly private siloes it per team.

Front:
Beyond apps and actions, how does the GitHub Marketplace benefit the developer community?

A) It provides a central place to discover both free and paid tools that integrate with and extend GitHub workflows
B) It hosts the only official copy of every open-source repository, replacing the need to clone projects individually
C) It guarantees that all listed tools are maintained by GitHub itself and therefore never require any security review
Back:
A) It provides a central place to discover both free and paid tools that integrate with and extend GitHub workflows

The Marketplace centralizes discovery of community and partner tools that extend GitHub for many workflows.

Reference: About GitHub Marketplace - GitHub Docs
Extra: Listings come from many publishers, not just GitHub, so you still evaluate trust and permissions. It aids discovery, not code hosting.

Front:
Which statement correctly describes GitHub's paid product plans for accounts?

A) GitHub offers only a single paid plan, and every feature including advanced security is bundled into that one tier
B) GitHub offers Free, Team, and Enterprise plans, with higher tiers adding features like advanced administration and support
C) GitHub charges per repository created, so accounts are billed a separate recurring fee for every individual repository they own
Back:
B) GitHub offers Free, Team, and Enterprise plans, with higher tiers adding features like advanced administration and support

GitHub provides tiered plans (Free, Team, Enterprise) that unlock progressively more collaboration, administration, and support features.

Reference: GitHub's plans - GitHub Docs
Extra: Free already includes unlimited public and private repos with basic features. Higher tiers add controls like SAML SSO, advanced auditing, and support.
